title: SDK Onboarding, Chaos & Fastpatch Playbook
author: Priya Narang
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes a consolidated, low-latency response pattern for SDK onboarding incidents, telemetry-driven chaos experiments during ramp, and an auditable fastpatch workflow to restore developer experience (DX) quickly. It is intended for developer experience (DevX) engineers, SDK owners, on-call support, and solutions engineers.

Why this exists
----------------
- Onboarding surges and new SDK releases cause concentrated failure modes (telemetry gaps, breaking ctor changes, streaming regressions).
- Time-to-fix must be minimized to preserve PLG activation funnels and downstream Hosted API usage.
- This doc codifies: detection, triage, temporary mitigations (fastpatches), and durable fixes with postmortem and regression goldens.

Scope and when to use
---------------------
Use this playbook for:
1) New SDK release rollouts where sign-ups or sample-apps start failing at scale.
2) Sudden increase in support tickets tied to SDK errors (>= 30 tickets/hour or 5% error-rate delta for 15m).
3) Telemetry/observability regressions that block debugging (missing tokens, dropped spans).

Prerequisites
-------------
- On-call DevX and runtime engineers have access to: DevX Slack (#devx-oncall), PagerDuty, Grafana dashboards (devx-sdk-telemetry), Logstore queries (logtail/devx-sdk).
- Golden trace artifacts in storage: s3://redwood-goldens/sdk/goldens/YYYYMMDD/
- Canary cohort: <canary-tenant-id> and sample apps repo (git@github.com:redwood/devx-sample-apps.git).

SLOs & thresholds
------------------
- Activation funnel uptime: 99.5% (per-region) during business hours
- SDK critical error-rate: <0.5% on 1h rolling window (critical = non-retriable client errors)
- Time-to-fastpatch goal: 30 minutes from triage to mitigation deployed

Detection: Signals to watch
--------------------------
- Spike in support tickets tagged "sdk-install", "api-error", "streaming-nondeterminism"
- Grafana alert: devx_sdk_error_rate > 5x baseline (5m)
- Missing or truncated telemetry: > 50% span sampling drop for new release
- Canary-run failures: unit/integration sample fails > 3 consecutive runs

Initial triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
------------------------------------------
1) Capture scope and blast radius: affected SDK language(s), release version, region, percent users affected.
2) Attach a P0 tag in ticketing and post incident summary to #devx-oncall (short headline + immediate mitigations).
3) Identify whether failure is: install-time, runtime auth, streaming, or telemetry-only.
4) If reproducible, run local canary against canary-tenant and collect golden trace.

Triage decision tree (short)
---------------------------
- If install-time / packaging: -> fastpatch: pin prior artifact in package registries and publish rollback package (see Fastpatch steps).
- If auth/token/credential: -> rotate keys, add fallback check in client (local cache), escalate to security if customer tokens exposed.
- If streaming/regression (breaking API): -> publish temporary compat shim in CDN or patch server-side compatibility translation.
- If telemetry missing: -> enable verbose client-side logging and forward to debugging endpoint, create short-term retention increase for logs.

Fastpatch steps (goal: mitigate within 30 minutes)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Create an incident branch in the SDK repo named incident/fastpatch/<short-id>.
2) Choose minimal safe mitigation:
   - packaging: republish vX.Y.Z+hotfix as vX.Y.Z-hot.1 with revert of only failing change.
   - runtime: add feature-flagged fallback path (client-side) to skip new code path.
   - telemetry: add a verbose-telemetry config that re-enables legacy exporter.
3) Run smoke tests from sample-apps (focus on critical flows). Use: 
   ```
   ./scripts/canary-run --tenant <canary-tenant-id> --sdk ./dist/sdk.tgz --smoke-only
   ```
4) Create a signed, time-limited release and push to package registries with clear release notes and incident tag.
5) Announce to #devx-oncall and affected customers (via Solutions Eng) with guidance and ETA.

Rollback & traffic management
-----------------------------
- Prefer soft rollback (package pinning, feature flags) over hard rollback where possible.
- Use Canary flagging to route 10% traffic back to prior SDK behavior, evaluate for 15 minutes, then expand.
- For server-side compatibility shims, use runtime routing rules in the Gateway (owner: eng-serving-runtime).

Observability & runbook integrations
-----------------------------------
- Dashboard checklist (run during incident):
  - devx_sdk_error_rate (5m, 1m)
  - devx_activation_conversion (15m)
  - golden_trace_failures (daily-run count)
  - telemetry_span_drop_rate (5m)
- Logs to collect: client stderr, client HTTP request samples, server-side request-id logs, stream chunk headers. Tag logs with incident id: INC-<YYYYMMDD>-<short>.

Sample CLI snippets and code examples
------------------------------------
- Reproduce canary locally (node):
```
# install local tarball and run sample
npm install ./dist/redwood-sdk-1.4.2-hot.1.tgz
NODE_ENV=canary node sample-apps/chat-smoke.js
```
- Temp feature flag (Python SDK):
```
from redwood_sdk import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'), fallback_mode='legacy_exporter')
```

Post-incident durable fixes (next 7 days)
---------------------------------------
1) Write a regression test that covers the broken path; add to CI matrix with the problematic environment.
2) Create a model/eval if quality drift is suspected (owner: applied-ml-and-evals).
3) Schedule an SDK patch release with integration tests and a staged rollout plan.
4) Add a telemetry golden and a daily smoke that runs prior to major releases.

Telemetry golden & regression guard template
------------------------------------------
| Name | Trigger | Acceptance | Owner | Run cadence |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| sdk-install-smoke | Post-publish | 0 install failures on canary | DevX SDK owner | Every publish + daily |
| stream-compat-golden | PR merge | 5 consecutive success runs | Eng Serving Runtime | Nightly |

Postmortem & blameless review template
--------------------------------------
- Summary: 1–2 sentences describing impact.
- Timeline: bullet timeline of key events (detection, triage start, fastpatch deploy, full fix).
- Root cause: short paragraph.
- Corrective actions: list of durable fixes, owners, and target dates.
- Lessons learned: operational changes (dashboards, alerts, docs).
- Follow-ups: link to PRs, tests added, and customer communication.

Ownership & escalation matrix
----------------------------
- DevX lead on-call: first responder for SDK-level issues.
- Eng-Serving-Runtime: for streaming and runtime routing fixes.
- Security: if tokens/credentials are implicated.
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success: customer-facing comms and mitigation guidance.

Appendix A: Quick reference table
--------------------------------
| Symptom | Immediate action | Owner | Fastpatch example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Package publish failures | Pin to previous artifact, republish hotfix | SDK owner | Publish v1.2.3-hot.1 |
| Streaming nondeterminism | Enable compat shim on gateway | Eng-Serving-Runtime | Add translation plugin |
| Telemetry gap | Re-enable legacy exporter & increase log retention | DevX Oncall | Toggle env var FALLBACK_TELEMETRY=1 |

Appendix B: Communication templates
-----------------------------------
- Slack incident banner (short):
  "P0: SDK onboarding errors impacting new signups in us-west. Investigating — using incident/fastpatch/20250912-01. Triage lead: Priya N. ETA for mitigation: 25m."
- Customer notice example (for Solutions Eng):
  "We detected an issue with the 1.4.2 SDK that can cause streaming errors for new installs. We have a temporary release (1.4.2-hot.1) available now that restores behavior while we prepare a durable fix. If you need assistance switching, reply and we will provide runbook steps."

Governance & review cadence
---------------------------
- Any fastpatch that changes public SDK surface must have a follow-up PR within 24 hours documenting the change and the rollback plan.
- Quarterly chaos/upgrade drills: DevX + Eng Serving Runtime should run at least one controlled release drill per quarter.

-----------------
